title: DR1 requires every identifier its commodity defines before an animal counts as identified; the frontend accepts any one of them

finding.frontend: Every identifier obligation is declared optional in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js:113-198, and the animal record above them requires only that one of the six is filled — `requires.anyOfIds` at :88-102, error code `obligation.unitRecord.identifiersRequired`. The save path matches: src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/animal-identification/form/forms.js:22-23 counts a card as holding data when a single box is non-empty, and :124-135 raises the "at least one identifier" error only when the whole card is blank. So a cow entered with an ear tag and nothing else is a complete animal, and the passport and tattoo boxes can be left empty for good. fe-animal-identification-saved shows exactly that: a saved cattle animal whose whole summary reads "Ear tag: UK123456789012".
finding.prototype: DR1 treats an animal as identified only when every field its commodity defines carries a value — `isAnimalIdentifierEntryComplete` in app/routes.js:1526-1532 tests `fields.every(...)`. A cattle animal saved with an ear tag but no passport does not advance the counter and does not appear in the saved list: the panel's active animal stays on the same index (:1590-1603) and the saved rows are filtered to complete entries only (:1621-1624). The user is pushed back to the same box until both are filled, and the identification task row stays Todo until every animal on every species has every field (:1534-1563).
finding.difference: Change the animal record's requirement from any-one-of to all-applicable: the six identifier obligations become mandatory where their commodity gate applies, and the `anyOfIds` requirement in identifiers.js:88-102 is replaced by per-field required errors. That means a required-field message per empty identifier rather than one "at least one identifier" message, so the error copy in the commodities copy file needs a per-field entry, and the empty-form guard in forms.js:124-135 is superseded. Check first whether the free-text fallback pair — Identification details and Animal description — should both become mandatory under the same rule, since DR1 has no commodity that pairs two free-text identifiers. Decide also which of DR1's two rules to mirror: its completeness rule is all-fields, but its submit gate is looser and demands identifiers only when more than one species is on the notification.
finding.falsifiedBy: Saving a DR1 cattle animal with an ear tag and an empty passport and seeing it appear in the saved-animals list with the counter advancing to the next animal.
finding.verification: Opened both rendered DOMs and the fe-animal-identification-saved and fe-animal-identification-at-maximum screenshots — the frontend's saved cattle rows carry an ear tag and nothing else, so one identifier is plainly enough. Read identifiers.js:88-102 and :113-198, forms.js:22-23 and :124-135, and on the DR1 side routes.js:1526-1532, :1588-1603, :1621-1624 and :1534-1563. Ran the falsifier through DR1's save path rather than the browser: isAnimalIdentifierEntryComplete uses fields.every, the active-animal loop stops at the first incomplete index, and completeSavedAnimals filters incomplete entries out of the saved list, so a cattle animal with an ear tag and no passport neither advances the counter nor joins the list. CORRECT.
finding.correction: Two line ranges were a line or two out and are corrected in place — the completeSavedAnimals filter is app/routes.js:1621-1624, given as :1622-1625, and the active-animal loop is :1590-1603, given as :1585-1603. Neither changes the claim. One thing was understated and is now named in the prose: DR1's own submit gate is looser than its completeness rule. requiresAnimalIdentifiersForSubmit at app/routes.js:1511-1513 demands identifiers only when more than one species is selected, so a single-species DR1 notification can be submitted with no identifier entries at all, while the identification task row still reads Todo until every field of every animal is filled. The finding's claim is about what counts as a complete animal, which is unconditional in DR1, so it stands; whoever picks up the obligation change has to decide which of the two DR1 rules to mirror, and finding.difference now says so.
